          # The `subagents` registry and its spawn/fork backends live in the HOST
          # composition: the registry is a process singleton whose cross-session queries
          # the api-proxy serves to the browser, and a provider name may only be
          # registered once. This preset contributes the delegation TOOLS, which resolve
          # that host registry.
          #
          # `workflows` is different — nothing outside an agent reads it — so every row
          # that reaches it shares one entry-local realm here, and a consumer left
          # outside would resolve a host registry this preset does not populate.
          #
          # `tool-subagent-report` is host-plane for the same reason as the registry,
          # not because a preset may not want it: it registers a CONTINUABLE SETUP on
          # that singleton rather than a tool this agent calls, and the setup list is
          # not scope-aware — one copy per mounted preset means every child gets
          # `report` registered once per live session, which throws on the second.
          - id: delegation
            name: cordis:group
            group: true
            isolate:
              workflowEngine: true
            config:
              - id: tool-subagent-control
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent-control'

              - id: tool-subagent
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
                config:
                  provider: spawn
                  toolName: subagent
                  # Model-facing opt-in: the model may name provider/model from the
                  # authorized list; omitting them still inherits the parent route.
                  # `modelDiscovery` registers the read-only `list_subagent_models`
                  # (one discovery owner per tool scope), the same pair the shipped
                  # standard preset mounts.
                  modelSelection: true
                  modelDiscovery: true

              - id: tool-subagent-fork
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
                config:
                  provider: fork
                  toolName: subagent_fork

              # One terminal line per delegated child: `subagent <id> route
              # <provider>/<model>`. Nothing else reports which model a child
              # ended up on — a route is named by the call, or inherited.
              - id: subagent-route-log
                name: 'dsh-more-agent-presets/presets/shared/subagent-route-log.mjs'
                config:
                  presetId: qwencode-coding-agent

              # Product providers are host-plane singletons. Copy this preset, then
              # remove `disabled` from either ordinary tool row to expose that product
              # only to agents composed from the copy.
              - id: tool-subagent-codex
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
                disabled: true
                config:
                  provider: codex
                  toolName: subagent_codex
                  maxDepth: provider-managed

              - id: tool-subagent-claude-code
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
                disabled: true
                config:
                  provider: claude-code
                  toolName: subagent_claude_code
                  maxDepth: provider-managed

              - id: workflow-ptc
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-workflow-ptc'
                config:
                  provider: spawn

              - id: tool-workflow
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-workflow'

              - id: tool-ralph
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-ralph'
                config:
                  subagentProvider: spawn
                  maxRounds: 64

          # ── remaining model-facing rows ─────────────────────────────────────────────

          - id: tool-ask-user
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-ask-user'

          - id: tool-todo
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-todo'
            config:
              allowParallelInProgress: true

          # The `web` service and its search provider stay in the host composition; only
          # the model-facing tool is per-session.
          - id: tool-web
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-web'
            config:
              fetch: false
              searchTimeoutMs: 60000

# Agent preset chat-agent: one `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset` declaration.
#
# A pure-conversation preset: its `config.plugins` list contains NO model-facing
# tool row, so the preset contributes no tool itself. The `no-tools` row covers
# both tool planes for these agents -- `ctx.tools.restrict({ allow: [] })` from
# the preset's standing scope (the scope every selecting Agent is parented to)
# masks the INHERITED surface, i.e. the deployment-global tool layer (`present`,
# `plugin_manager`, a profile's extra host tool plugins), and
# `ctx.tools.guard(...)` refuses execution of anything registered in the agent's
# OWN scope, which no restriction can reach (Team tools on a profile that mounts
# `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-agent-team-profile` still get LISTED -- see
# `no-tools.mjs` and CHANGELOG 1.6.1). Do not "complete" this list with tool rows.
#
# The persona comes from `model-persona.mjs` (it replaces the
# `@deepseek-ai/dsh-persona` row): the text is picked per session model -- the
# model the Session selected (`pending ?? lastUsed` of its `modelSelection`
# projection, else `agent.options.model`) -- from the verbatim table in
# `presets/shared/model-personas.json`, which the plugin reads itself at
# apply time. The row below carries NO `config`: the JSON file is the only copy
# of the table, so there is nothing to keep in sync. The persona keeps
# `complete: true` semantics (the picked text IS the whole system prompt: no
# tool guidance, no skill catalog, no harness identity) and runtime-context
# suppression (no `Current runtime context` user-role snapshot and no
# `context()` blocks), which the plugin performs as its two calls.
#
# The compaction group keeps automatic (pressure / context-overflow) compaction
# and the human `/compact` command: a chat session is long by nature. It omits
# `tool-result-pruner` on purpose -- with no tool rows there are no tool results
# to prune, and `compaction-basic` reads `toolResultPruner` through an optional
# `ctx.get`, so the group composes without it.
#
# A pure `insert` with no `!!js` expression: nothing here is platform- or
# environment-conditional.
- insert:
    - id: preset-chat-agent
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset'
      config:
        id: chat-agent
        order: 15
        name: "通用聊天模式"
        description: "纯聊天助手：不调用任何工具，只专注对话本身。"
        plugins:
          # `no-tools.mjs` masks the inherited plane and refuses the rest (header).
          - id: no-tools
            name: 'dsh-more-agent-presets/presets/chat-agent/no-tools.mjs'

          # `model-persona.mjs` replaces the `@deepseek-ai/dsh-persona` row:
          # it picks the persona text per session model and makes it the
          # complete system prompt. The text is NOT here: the plugin reads
          # `presets/shared/model-personas.json` (the only copy) itself. It sits
          # in `presets/shared/` because `chat-subagent` reads the same table;
          # `presets/chat-agent/model-persona.mjs` is only a re-export shim kept
          # for overrides written against the pre-1.7.0 path.
          - id: model-persona
            name: 'dsh-more-agent-presets/presets/shared/model-persona.mjs'

          # `token-meter` stays host-plane and is resolved from here; only the
          # compaction provider and its only consumer (`command-compact`) share
          # this realm.
          - id: compaction
            name: cordis:group
            group: true
            isolate:
              compaction: true
            config:
              - id: compaction-basic
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-basic'
              - id: command-compact
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-command-compact'

# Agent preset chat-subagent: one `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset` declaration,
# derived from `presets/chat-agent.patch.yml`.
#
# The rule this preset exists to break: `chat-agent` can call nothing, this one
# can call ONE thing that starts work — `subagent`, the tool that creates a
# subagent to carry the task out — plus the read-only `list_subagent_models` the
# `modelDiscovery` option registers, which only reports the routes the session
# may name. A deployment that mounts the agent-team bundle still LISTS its nine
# Team tools in the top-level catalog (own-layer registrations no mask can hide),
# and the guard refuses every one of them. The delegated subagent is a real agent
# with a real (read-only) tool set; the top-level session is the delegator. A
# depth-0 catalog MASK narrows the top-level catalog to the two delegation names
# (the own-layer Team rows cannot be hidden), and the guard refuses every call
# outside those names.
#
# WHY NO RESTRICTION ON THE PRESET PLANE, AND WHY THE MASK IS ON THE AGENT. The
# obvious shape — a preset-plane `ctx.tools.restrict({ allow: [] })` next to
# these rows — is wrong, and silently so: a delegated child JOINS ITS PARENT'S
# PRESET (`applyChildComposition` → `agentPresets.composeFrom(childCtx,
# parent.ctx)`, `packages/subagent/subagent/src/child-agent.ts:200-219`), and
# the standing scope's restriction is on the child's chain too, so the child
# would inherit the same empty catalog and the delegation would accomplish
# nothing. A restriction can only narrow, so no later composition can undo it.
# The mask therefore lives on ONE agent's OWN scope and only at depth 0
# (`delegator.mjs` point 5): `ToolRuntime.view()` filters only the surface a
# scope INHERITS, so a per-agent restriction narrows the preset's inherited rows
# without touching the child, whose scope parent is the standing scope rather
# than the parent Agent's scope (`agent-preset-registry/src/index.ts:171-176`,
# join `:317-329`).
# The mask is an ALLOW-LIST of the two delegation names: since 0.2.2-rc.1 the
# delegation tools are registered on the preset's standing layer (the per-Agent
# install is gone), so they are inherited like every other row and an empty
# allow-list would hide them too. It is a CATALOG mask, not enforcement:
# `restrict()` hides names, and the standing GUARD (point 6) refuses every call
# outside those names (the two delegation tools; every Team tool a deployment's
# agent-team bundle lists stays refused). `delegator.mjs` carries the mechanism
# with source pointers.
#
# WHY THE MASK INSTALLS ONE MACROTASK LATE. Measured, 1.7.3 live on `dev_web`:
# `restrict()` notifies `tools/change`, and the 0.2.1 line's official delegation
# plugin installed into a live Agent on exactly that event — an agent-scope
# restriction installed synchronously from `agent/created` gave one scope two
# installs, the second threw `tool "list_subagent_models" is already registered
# in this scope`, its `install()` aborted before `mount()`, and the session got
# NO delegation tool at all. 0.2.2-rc.1 removed that per-Agent install path
# entirely, so the collision cannot recur per the 0.2.2-rc.1 sources (a live
# switch on an rc.1 host is not yet measured), but the mask is still coalesced into
# one `setTimeout(..., 0)` flush: `restrict()` must not notify inside the
# creation or switch dispatch that asked for it, and a named allow-list can only
# be installed after the delegation rows are registered. Lifting is deferred the
# same way, so leaving the preset restores the rows. That flush runs one
# macrotask after the dispatch, which is why a catalog read taken inside the
# same tick as `sessionController.create` still shows the inherited rows.
#
# WHY THESE TOOL ROWS. On the `web` profile the host plane's model-facing rows
# are all disabled (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app` `cordis.patch.yml:430-556`), so
# what an agent sees is exactly what its preset mounts, and the child inherits
# this preset's rows like the root session does. These four rows are the
# only source of the names `subagentTools` lists: `read` (plus `write`/`edit`,
# which the guard refuses for both agents), `glob`/`grep`, `todo_write`, and the
# `job_*` family. `write`/`edit`/`bash` are deliberately
# out of the default list: the subagent works read-only in this release (see
# TODO.md for the writable/command-capable follow-up).
#
# Two names in `subagentTools` are NOT ours and may be absent from a deployment:
# `read_image` registers only while an attachment store is mounted
# (`packages/fs/tool-fs/src/index.ts:67-72`), and `list_directory` comes from a
# third-party profile row. Nothing probes for them any more: the guard allows
# those names, and a name that is not registered is simply not in the catalog, so
# a missing tool costs that tool and never the delegation.
#
# THE ONE TOOL THAT STARTS WORK. `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent` mounts one
# model-facing delegation tool per instance, on the `spawn` provider (a fresh
# child that never sees this conversation, so a task prompt must stand alone).
# DSH 0.2.1 deleted `backgroundMode` and `enableRunInBackground` outright: every
# delegation is a MANAGED ACTIVATION (`ctx.subagents.startActivation`), so the
# call returns `{ kind: 'activation', subagentId }` at once instead of the
# child's report, there is no `run_in_background` parameter left to remove, and
# the runtime delivers the child's final answer to THIS session as a settlement
# notice (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent` `src/manager.ts`, `notifySettlement` →
# `createSettlementMessage`). Nothing collects a child through
# `job_output`/`job_kill` any more — those remain ordinary background-JOB tools.
# `maxDepth: 1` states the recursion budget outright: the child may not delegate
# again (the guard's child branch keeps only the read-only names and does not
# include `subagent`).
#
# WHY `modelSelection` + `modelDiscovery` HERE TOO. `modelSelection` adds the
# optional `provider`/`model`/`reasoning_effort` parameters to `subagent`, and
# `modelDiscovery` registers the read-only `list_subagent_models` that reads the
# Session's authorized routes — so a chat session can name the child's model like
# the five coding presets do. The two are separate switches on 0.2.2; the old
# `modelSelectionSettings` flag did both jobs and is gone. Registration no longer
# moves per Agent: the delegation tools and the lister live on this preset's
# STANDING layer, which every Agent of the preset inherits — which is exactly why
# the depth-0 mask must allow-list the two names (see above). The Host row
# `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent/model-selection-settings` still supplies the
# authorized route list; without it the opt-in mounts and explicit selection is
# limited to the parent route instead of failing the whole preset (the 0.2.1
# behaviour). The five coding presets carry the same pair, so the only difference
# is that this preset may CALL one of the tools it lists.
#
# WHY THE DELEGATION ROW IS INSIDE A `cordis:group`. Measured on 0.2.1, 2026-10-18:
# a preset switch is `agentPresets.select` → `recompose` (a scope rebind plus ONE
# `tools/change`), and the 0.2.1 line's per-Agent install of the INCOMING preset
# raced the asynchronous disposal of the OUTGOING one. Their order is listener
# order, which is preset MOUNT order, and a top-level row mounts before the rows
# of a `cordis:group`: a top-level delegation row put this preset FIRST among the
# eleven `tools/change` listeners (measured index 2, before `standard` at 3), so
# every switch INTO this preset registered `list_subagent_models` while
# `standard`'s copy was still there — the duplicate threw, `install()` aborted
# before `mount()`, the failed fiber stayed cached in `scopedInstalls`, and the
# session kept NEITHER tool. Inside this group the listener registered LATE
# (after every other preset's), the outgoing removal ran first, and the switch
# succeeded. 0.2.2-rc.1 removed that per-Agent install path, so the race and the
# `scopedInstalls` cache are gone; the row stays inside the group because it is
# the shape the five coding presets mount and moving it back buys nothing. Do
# not move it out without re-measuring a preset switch on the new host.
#
# The top-level persona text is NOT here: `delegator.mjs` composes it from the
# shared table `chat-agent` also reads (`presets/shared/model-personas.json`, via
# `presets/shared/model-persona.mjs`) plus the delegation note it reads from
# `presets/chat-subagent/delegation-note.md`. One table, one note, each in one
# file.
#
# The CHILD's persona moved OFF the delegation row in the 0.2.1 upgrade:
# `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent` now REJECTS a `persona` (and `toolFilter`)
# config with a hard throw, because a child's identity and tool set come only
# from the Agent Preset it composes. `subagent-persona` below is that
# preset-plane row. Omission of `agentPreset` is what makes it reach the child:
# the provider calls `agentPresets.composeFrom(childCtx, parent.ctx)`, so the
# child joins THIS preset's standing scope and keeps both the read-only tool rows
# and the standing guard, while the preset-plane `deployment:persona-prefix`
# lands in its prompt. The root session is unaffected: the `delegator` row
# registers the SAME section name on each depth-0 AGENT's own scope with
# `complete: true`, and a nearer scope wins a section name
# (`ScopedLayers.merge`, farthest ancestor first), so the root keeps the
# per-model persona + delegation note and only a child reads this row. The one
# deliberate cost: this row's default empty `suffix` also shadows the
# deployment's persona suffix for the child scope.
#
# A pure `insert` with no `!!js` expression: nothing here is platform- or
# environment-conditional.
- insert:
    - id: preset-chat-subagent
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset'
      config:
        id: chat-subagent
        order: 16
        name: "通用聊天模式 · 可派活"
        description: "顶层只放行 subagent 与 list_subagent_models（可为子 agent 指定模型）；其余工具一律拒绝：让只读子 agent 收集证据，你据此自行判断并回答。"
        plugins:
          # The delegation guard, the depth-0 catalog mask and the delegator
          # persona. `presetId` must equal this declaration's `id` (it is what
          # tells the plugin which live agents belong to this preset during
          # `tools/change` reconciliation); `subagentTools` is the single source
          # of the child's read-only list.
          # An optional `delegationNote` here would REPLACE the shipped
          # `delegation-note.md` for this preset; the shipped declaration sets
          # neither, so the file is what the session's prompt ends with.
          - id: delegator
            name: 'dsh-more-agent-presets/presets/chat-subagent/delegator.mjs'
            config:
              presetId: chat-subagent
              subagentTools:
                - read
                - glob
                - grep
                - read_image
                - list_directory
                - todo_write
                - job_list

          # The CHILD's own persona, as a preset-plane row (0.2.1: the
          # delegation row may no longer carry one). It shadows the deployment
          # persona for every scope of this preset except a depth-0 agent, whose
          # `delegator` section wins the name. See "The CHILD's persona moved OFF
          # the delegation row" in this file's header.
          - id: subagent-persona
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-persona'
            config:
              prefix: |-
                You are a delegated read-only evidence collector for a chat session. You cannot see
                the conversation that produced your task, so the task prompt is all you have. Work
                only through the tools in your catalog and keep the investigation tight.

                Collect evidence; do not answer the user's question or make the delegating agent's
                decision. Reply with a compact report it can judge:
                - what you were asked to establish;
                - what you inspected: file paths, line numbers, and exact snippets;
                - what you observed, kept separate from anything you inferred;
                - what you could not determine, and any evidence that conflicts;
                - optional interpretations, clearly labelled as hypotheses.

                Never invent an observation, and never present a conclusion as established when
                your evidence does not support it. You cannot run commands, modify files, or
                delegate further.

          # The one model-facing tool that acts (header). It sits inside a
          # group on purpose: see "WHY THE DELEGATION ROW IS INSIDE A GROUP".
          - id: delegation
            name: cordis:group
            group: true
            isolate:
              workflowEngine: true
            config:
              - id: tool-subagent
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
                config:
                  provider: spawn
                  toolName: subagent
                  maxDepth: 1
                  # Model-facing opt-in: `provider` / `model` / `reasoning_effort`
                  # on `subagent`, plus the read-only `list_subagent_models` via
                  # `modelDiscovery` (one discovery owner per tool scope).
                  # Authorized routes come from the Host's
                  # `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent/model-selection-settings` row
                  # when the profile mounts it; without that row the opt-in still
                  # mounts and explicit selection is limited to the parent route.
                  modelSelection: true
                  modelDiscovery: true

          # The child's tool sources. The depth-0 mask hides them from the
          # top-level catalog; the guard also refuses a call to one, so a hidden
          # name can never act.
          - id: tool-fs
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs'
          - id: tool-fs-search
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs-search'
            config:
              sampleOverCapGlobResults: false
          - id: tool-todo
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-todo'
            # The one key this plugin has no default for (`allowParallelInProgress`
            # is `.required()` in its Config), so a row without it fails to mount
            # and the WHOLE preset reports a load failure. The shipped standard
            # preset passes `true`; this row mirrors that.
            config:
              allowParallelInProgress: true
          - id: tool-jobs
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-jobs'

          # A chat session is long by nature, and a child that greps a repository
          # produces the large tool results the pruner exists for; the top-level
          # session has none, so the row costs it nothing.
          - id: compaction
            name: cordis:group
            group: true
            isolate:
              compaction: true
              toolResultPruner: true
            config:
              - id: compaction-basic
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-basic'
              - id: command-compact
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-command-compact'
              - id: tool-result-pruner
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-tool-result-pruner'
                config:
                  thresholdChars: 8192
                  headChars: 4096
                  tailChars: 1024

[中文文档](README.zh.md)

Multiple selectable Agent Presets for DeepSeek Harness.

The presets are adapted for DeepSeek Harness (DSH).

This plugin is particularly useful for:

**Non-DeepSeek or Older Models:**
- Improves performance for models that haven't been specifically adapted for DSH
- Enhances older models that lack DSH-specific adaptations

**Personal Preference:**
- Some users may prefer more interactive, discussion-based coding assistance over independent work

**Why It Helps:**
- DSH's default prompts are optimized for DeepSeek models
- Non-DeepSeek or older models may not perform optimally with default prompts
- These presets provide alternative interaction patterns suitable for different models
A professional coding assistant emphasizing code standards and project conventions, using iterative workflows and CLI-friendly interaction style.

An interactive CLI agent with dynamic environment awareness, automatic Git context injection, and structured task workflows. Features auto-detected platform information, security-first permissions handling, and CLI-optimized communication style.

An enhanced mode for creating custom Agent presets. Includes all standard capabilities plus runtime inspection, plugin experimentation, and preset authoring guidance.

**Features:**
- DSH context information (Web UI URL, source root)
- Git repository awareness
- Custom prompt sections
- Skills for Cordis plugin development and composition editing

**Current Limitation:**
⚠️ Cordis Tool (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-cordis`) is currently unavailable due to upstream issues. Dynamic Cordis plugin creation will be available after upstream fixes.

A coding assistant that works alongside the user as a pair programmer: aligns direction before each move, discusses before non-trivial edits, and waits for confirmation rather than driving the task to completion on its own.

A port of the open-source Codex CLI agent prompt: it states what it is about to do before each tool call, reads the codebase before editing, and drives the task to completion on its own, following Codex's planning, validation, and final-answer formatting rules. Tool names are mapped to this harness's tools (`apply_patch` → `edit`/`write`, `update_plan` → `todo_write`, `request_user_input` → `ask_user_question`), and Codex's plan-mode protocol is preserved through `exit_plan_mode`. The three Codex `input[]` blocks — `<permissions instructions>`, `<collaboration_mode>`, and `<environment_context>` — are injected as user-role messages at the head of every admitted step via three DSH `agent/pre-step` plugins (`codex-permissions.mjs`, `codex-collab-mode.mjs`, `codex-environment.mjs`), with the live sandbox / approval policy and cwd / platform / shell / date resolved from the DSH runtime. Unlike the other presets here, this one keeps Codex's autonomous posture rather than a discussion-first one.

A pure-conversation assistant: it mounts no tool row, masks every **inherited** tool through a preset-plane `ctx.tools.restrict({ allow: [] })`, and refuses execution of anything registered in the agent's **own** scope through a `ctx.tools.guard(...)` — so it cannot act: no reading or writing files, no commands, no web search, no spawning a teammate. Two boundaries are deliberate and documented (`presets/chat-agent/no-tools.mjs` has the mechanism with source pointers). First, a preset-plane restriction covers the inherited surface only — the global layer plus every ancestor scope — while an agent's own registrations are exempt; a profile that mounts such a plugin, e.g. `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-agent-team-profile` (whose nine Team tools go into `agent.ctx` for every root agent), therefore still **lists** them in that session's tool catalog, and the guard is what makes their call return a refusal instead of running. Second, that refusal is not the `unknown tool` a filtered tool produces. **The system prompt switches with the current model** (Default / Codex GPT-5 · GPT-6 / Qwen / DeepSeek-R1 / Gemini 3.7 · 3.8 texts; the verbatim table lives in `presets/shared/model-personas.js

A chat assistant whose whole capability is **one tool that STARTS work**: `subagent` — plus the read-only `list_subagent_models` the model-selection opt-in registers, which only reports the routes the session may name. The top-level session's tool **catalog holds exactly those two delegation names from this preset**: a depth-0 catalog mask — `ctx.tools.restrict({ allow: ['subagent', 'list_subagent_models'] })` on the Agent's own scope, installed by `presets/chat-subagent/delegator.mjs` — narrows the preset's inherited rows to those two names. Since DSH 0.2.2-rc.1 the delegation tools are registered on the preset's standing layer (the per-Agent install is gone), so the mask allow-lists them instead of relying on the old own-layer exemption. Hiding is not enforcement: one standing guard — `ctx.tools.guard(...)`, installed once on the preset's standing plane by the same plugin — refuses every call outside those names (the two delegation tools; the Team tools a deployment's bundle lists are refused too). The mask sits on the Agent scope, so a delegated child never inherits it (the child's scope parent is the preset's standing scope); the guard is read from the **calling** agent's chain

**The delegated subagent is what actually works, and it works read-only.** A delegated child **joins its parent's preset**, so it inherits the same rows — and the same guard, whose depth branch is what bounds it: the child may call the declaration's `subagentTools` list — by default `read`, `glob`, `grep`, `read_image`, `list_directory`, `todo_write`, `job_list` — and nothing else. There is no `bash`, `write`, or `edit` in that list: the subagent investigates and reports, and cannot run commands, run tests, or change files (`TODO.md` tracks the writable follow-up). Two of those names are deployment-dependent — `read_image` exists only while an attachment store is mounted, and `list_directory` comes from a third-party profile plugin — and nothing probes for them any more: the guard judges by the declared list, so a name no row registered is simply absent from the catalog. The mask is on the parent Agent's scope, never on the preset plane, for exactly this reason: a preset-plane restriction would be on the child's chain too (it joins the same preset) and a restriction can only narrow, so the child could not undo it.

**The system prompt switches with the current model.** It is the shared table (`presets/shared/model-personas.json`, read through `presets/shared/model-persona.mjs`, which `chat-agent` mounts as its own prompt) plus a delegation note (`presets/chat-subagent/delegation-note.md`, read verbatim when the row mounts), and together they are the session's **entire** prompt. Automatic (pressure / overflow) compaction, the human `/compact` command, and tool-result pruning stay on: the child greps repositories, so its tool results need pruning even though the top-level session produces none.

The note defines the **delegation contract**: the child only collects evidence — observations, paths and line numbers, exact snippets, what it could not determine, and any conflicting evidence — and does not answer for the user; the top-level session makes the judgment, never forwards the user's request verbatim, never presents the child's conclusion as its own answer, and starts a narrower probe when the evidence is thin. The two halves live in `presets/chat-subagent/delegation-note.md` (top level) and the `subagent-persona` row of `presets/chat-subagent.patch.yml` (child). The guard and mask can only decide what is callable, so this step is constrained by prompt text alone.

**Changing the subagent's tool list** means overriding the declaration by its Loader row id in a profile patch. `config` is replaced wholesale, so every row must be restated; the list is the guard's allow-list for the child, so a name no row registers is simply not in the catalog:

```yaml

- id: preset-chat-subagent
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset'
  config:
    id: chat-subagent
    order: 16
    name: "通用聊天模式 · 可派活"
    description: "顶层只放行 subagent 与 list_subagent_models（可为子 agent 指定模型）：把任务交给只读子 agent 去查、去读，自己专注对话。"
    plugins:
      - id: delegator
        name: 'dsh-more-agent-presets/presets/chat-subagent/delegator.mjs'
        config:
          presetId: chat-subagent
          subagentTools: [read, glob, grep, todo_write]
      # …every remaining row of the shipped declaration, unchanged…
```

Widening that list does not rewrite the delegation note: the note is the file `presets/chat-subagent/delegation-note.md`, read verbatim when the row mounts, and it describes the shipped read-only default — revise the file when the child's abilities change, or override it for one profile with the `delegator` row's `delegationNote`. Nothing reads the tool list out of the note: it says in prose what the subagent can and cannot do.

One boundary is deliberate and stays: a profile that mounts the agent-team bundle still **lists** its nine Team tools for the top-level session, because an agent's own registrations are exempt from any restriction — the depth-0 mask cannot hide them. **None of them is callable here.** They address Team members, and the child this preset starts is not one: `list_agents` reports only the session itself, `send_message` to any of those names is refused, and the child still answers with a completion notice. Admitting `list_agents` / `send_message` (1.8.1) was measured to loop: a model that had just started a child polled `wait_agent` eight times, listed itself, messaged itself, and started the same task twice more while the first child was still running. The preset's own `read`/`write`/`todo_*`/`job_*` rows, by contrast, are hidden from that catalog by the mask and refused by the guard if a call is attempted anyway. And `job_list` is inert for the subagent — it cannot start a job — but it is part of the default list so that the writable follow-up needs no second edit.

The five coding presets and `chat-subagent` opt into the Host's subagent model-selection surface with `modelSelection: true` and `modelDiscovery: true` on their delegation row — the same two switches the shipped `standard`/`ptc`/`cordis` presets carry since DSH 0.2.2-rc.1, where the pre-0.2.2 `modelSelectionSettings` flag was renamed and split in two. The top-level Agent then gets two things:

- **`list_subagent_models`** reports the routes this session may use. No arguments list the authorized providers, `provider` lists that provider's advertised models, and `provider` + `model` adds that model's reasoning efforts.
- **`subagent`** gains the optional `provider`, `model`, and `reasoning_effort` parameters. Omit all three and the child still inherits the parent session's model — the official default, and exactly what these presets did before the opt-in.

The authorized list is the Host's `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent/model-selection-settings` row, i.e. the "Allow Agent to select a model for subagents" panel in the Web UI. An explicit route outside that list fails with a message naming the route (it does not list the available ones; call `list_subagent_models` for that). The list is sampled when a session is created, so it only affects new sessions. With the setting off (or its list empty) the behaviour falls back to inheritance without an error.

That row supplies the authorized list. The shipped `dsh-base` + `dsh-web-app` stack mounts it by default, and so do the profiles in this repository. Since DSH 0.2.2-rc.1 it is no longer a mount dependency: without it the opt-in still mounts and explicit selection is limited to the parent route (the lister falls back to it too), so a missing row costs the wider list, not the whole preset.

`chat-subagent` opts in too, so a chat session can name the child's model like the coding presets do. Its top-level catalog is not empty — the two delegation names, plus the nine Team tools when the deployment mounts the agent-team bundle — and only one of them can be called to start work, which is why its invariant reads "exactly one tool that STARTS work". Since DSH 0.2.2-rc.1 the delegation tools stay on the preset's standing plane (the opt-in no longer installs into each Agent's own layer), so every Agent inherits them; that is why the depth-0 mask allow-lists the two names (see the preset section above) instead of relying on an own-layer exemption. `chat-agent` mounts no tool row at all, so it has nothing to opt in.

`chat-subagent` differs on one point: its standing guard refuses a depth-0 `subagent` call that names neither `provider` nor `model` whenever the authorized list holds at least one route, so a session that never called `list_subagent_models` cannot delegate silently on the inherited route. With no list to name — the opt-in off, an empty list, or a policy this build cannot read — omission stays legal and the child inherits the parent route. The five coding presets keep the official omit-to-inherit behaviour: their delegation note asks for a named route, and nothing refuses its absence.

**Which model a child actually ran on is a terminal line.** Every delegation prints one, from `presets/shared/subagent-route-log.mjs` — mounted by these five presets — or from `chat-subagent`'s own `delegator`:

```
[I] pair-coding-agent/subagent-route-log: subagent 3f1c… route opencode-chat/deepseek-v4.1-flash
[I] chat-subagent/delegator: subagent 3f1c… route opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash
```

The line names the route the child was created with, which is the route the call asked for or the one it inherited from the parent session; `unknown` appears only when the harness stated neither half. Top-level sessions print nothing.

**Two upstream warnings can appear around a short-lived child** and are cosmetic: `agent-registry … agent/disposed listener threw: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'catch')` (the tool chains `.catch` onto a `dispose()` that may return `undefined` — the per-Agent install path the opt-in activates) and `session-projection-cache … write for "…" failed (cache stays stale)` (a fail-soft race when a fast child's handle closes before a throttled checkpoint). `TODO.md` records the sources; the child's cached session record is in fact complete.

The plugin is a **declarative preset bundle**: installing it adds seven `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset` declaration rows to the profile through `dsh.bundle.patch` (one per preset, in `presets/<id>.patch.yml`). The declaration rows are registered with `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset-registry` and appear in the preset picker automatically. The plugin writes nothing to the user directory — no files are copied anywhere.

**Declarative presets (DSH 0.1.7+):**
- Each preset is a `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset` row declared in a bundle patch; `config.plugins` holds the child plugin rows (tools, prompt sections, groups with `isolate` realms, and the plugin's inline `.mjs` plugins referenced as package subpath exports under `dsh-more-agent-presets/presets/<id>/`, with assets shared by more than one preset under `dsh-more-agent-presets/presets/shared/`).
- Preset `id` values (`chat-agent`, `chat-subagent`, `codex-coding-agent`, `iflow-coding-agent`, `iflow-cre-agent`, `pair-coding-agent`, `qwencode-coding-agent`) are unchanged from previous releases, so existing session selections keep working. `chat-subagent` is the one row this bundle adds, and it is a new preset rather than a change to `chat-agent`.
- The registry retains each declaration's composition for live sessions; editing a declaration affects subsequently created Agents.

**Multi-file patch, the bundle's own row, and the root entry artifact:**
- `dsh.bundle.patch` is an **ordered list** (`cordis.patch.yml` plus one `presets/<id>.patch.yml` per preset) — the array form DSH core supports. A host composes all eight layers and, because this is a bundle, activation happens on the next start, not on hot mount.
- `cordis.patch.yml` declares the bundle's **own** loader row (`id`/`name`: `dsh-more-agent-presets`), and `index.mjs` is the no-op plugin behind it. That row is what makes the bundle visible in the running composition, and it is the shape every bundle uses for itself (`dshmarket` inserts `dsh-market` / `dshmarket`; `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app` inserts `web-runtime` / `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app`). Without it, `dshmarket`'s liveness check (`liveIncludes`) has nothing to match — the seven preset rows are named `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset` — and the plugin manager reports *"已安装，重启后生效"* on every page load, restart or not, while the presets keep working.
- Some third-party tooling only understands the string form of `dsh.bundle.patch`, and judges an installed build by its declared root entry artifact. `index.mjs` — declared through `main` and `exports[".

**Migration from ≤1.4.x:**
- Versions ≤1.4.4 copied preset directories into `$DSH_HOME/.agent-presets` (normally `~/.dsh/.agent-presets`) with a `.dsh-preset-owner.json` marker. DSH 0.1.7 no longer reads that directory, and this plugin no longer writes it.
- After upgrading, the old copied directories are inert leftovers. Remove them manually if you want a clean slate:
  ```bash
  rm -rf ~/.dsh/.agent-presets
  ```
  (Only your own `~/.dsh/.agent-presets`; nothing from another plugin or hand-authored presets should live there in the new mechanism, since presets are profile patches now.)

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-more-agent-presets
```

Removing the bundle removes its patch layer, so the seven preset declarations disappear from the profile. The preset `plugins` assets installed under the profile's node_modules are removed with the package. No `~/.dsh/.agent-presets` cleanup is needed on 0.1.7+ (see Behavior Notes if you are migrating from ≤1.4.x).
